The GPU Boom is running on a circular financing loop.

If you want to understand the economics of the AI sector, you need to look at Nvidia, CoreWeave, and Nebius.

Here is how the circular flow works:
1. Nvidia invests cash directly into specialized GPU cloud providers (like CoreWeave).
2. These cloud providers use the cash to purchase Nvidia's latest H100/B200 GPUs.
3. Nvidia records these purchases as record-breaking revenue, boosting its stock valuation.
4. The cloud providers use their newly acquired GPUs as collateral to raise more debt, buying even more chips.

While this engine has successfully scaled AI compute infrastructure at lightning speed, it creates a highly concentrated risk loop. If end-user demand for AI applications cools down, the specialized clouds won't be able to service their debt, and a massive supply of secondary GPUs will hit the market.

Are we looking at infrastructure buildout (similar to the telecom boom of the late 90s) or a financial bubble?
